title: Mum's Middle (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 96bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate unhurried
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The middle child gets good at watching
You learn to read a room before you speak
Corey never rushed the conversation
Just waited till it mattered and said it clean

[Verse 2]
He found the ocean in his own sweet time
Not rugby like his brother, that was never his
But give him salt air and an open morning
That's when I see my middle boy at his

[Chorus]
My middle one, the one who found his own
My middle one, the one who made a home
Not louder than the others, not behind
My middle one — you were exactly right

[Bridge]
He rang me once from somewhere near the water
Said Mum, I think I've worked it out
I said love, you worked it out when you were seven
You just needed time to let yourself have no doubt

[Verse 3]
He sends me music now and asks what I think
Songs about the family, songs about the day
I listen in the garden with my cup of tea
And think — there's my Corey finding his way

[Outro]
The gardens still growing
The gardens still growing
My middle one
The gardens still growing
